newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Coal gas research facility set up in Queensland.
newsitem.headline: Coal gas research facility set up in Queensland.

text.p: Australia's government said it was contributing funds towards a A$5 million coal gas research project being established in the state of Queensland.
"It is vital our major industry is at the forefront of the latest technology," Federal resources and energy minister Warwick Parer told a news conference on Thursday.

Parer said both the Australian government and Queensland's state government would contribute an equal share of A$1.2 million towards the project, supporting the A$1 million commitment of the coal industry and up to A$2.8 million from the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation
Coal is Australia's biggest export commodity and outranks all other exports unless the various categories of tourism revenue are treated collectively.

Parer said extensive research on advanced coal utilisation technologies currently being undertaken overseas, particularly in the United States, meant Australia had to know how Australian coals would perform under new technologies.

"It is projects such as this that ensures the Australian coal industry remains a leader in clean and efficient use of our high quality coal which in turn means continued reductions in emission levels both by domestic and international consumers," Parer said.
Executive director of CSIRO's research centre for black coal, John Hart said the research would help in efforts to make black coal as efficient and unobtrusive as natural gas.
The gasifier, to be established at Pinjarra Hills, near Ipswich, was expected to be fully commissioned by mid-1998.
